argument_summary: Certification is supportable only on a narrow current-documentation basis. The admissible record shows the release clears aggregate readiness by 2.4 points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which supports launch readiness at the overall level. But the same record also shows a current subgroup weakness in the health-plan benefits support slice and no approved mitigation or attached disclosure text. The defensible position is therefore not that prior approval covers this release, but that certification can proceed only if the current release documentation expressly discloses the current subgroup limitation.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit question. The admissible basis for certification should stand or fall on the current evidence and the documentation condition, not on launch-velocity considerations.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy is current-release specific. It allows certification only if current documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. The prior approval from nine weeks ago and the informal monitoring note can be treated as continuity context, but they do not satisfy the policy on their own. On this record, clean compliance is not supported; caveated compliance tied to explicit current disclosure is the strongest policy-consistent position.
concessions: The prior release approval is stale with respect to the current benefits corpus refresh and current evaluation batch.
The health-plan benefits support slice is 1.5 points below the warning threshold.
The release thread does not contain reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or attached disclosure language.
The record does not support treating the informal monitoring comment as approved risk acceptance.
